quantisation_bound: 5 mm per axis (1 cm position quantum, round-to-nearest); Euclidean <= 8.7 mm; exact against the quantised truth at every delivered tick
network: one-way delay uniform in [2.0, 12.0] ms +/- 1.5 ms jitter, loss 0.00% per packet
notes: The emitter owns the canon (10,000 seeded objects: random walks, circular orbits and a few fast movers) and a 10 m spatial hash, and it is viewpoint-agnostic: it knows each subscriber's interest region, not its camera. At every delivery it intersects the subscriber's moving region (a sphere or a perspective frustum) with the hash and sends only the difference from what that subscriber already holds: objects that entered the region (absolute quantised pose), objects that left (id only), and objects whose pose moved (a quantised delta). The pose delta is measured against what the projector can *predict* from the motion channel it already holds - a snapshot of position, velocity and time, extrapolated - so an object moving smoothly costs nothing at all, and the projector applies the identical prediction, so the two agree exactly. Positions are quantised to a 1 cm grid (round-to-nearest): a reconstruction is off by at most 5 mm per axis (8.7 mm Euclidean) and never drifts, because every delta is taken against the quantised truth, never against an accumulated estimate. Network: one-way delay uniform in [2.0, 12.0] ms +/- 1.5 ms jitter, loss 0.00% per packet. The receiver back-dates: it anchors each correction at the tick the correction was computed for, so the held state is the emitter's truth at that tick whatever the link did, and the reconstruction is checked against the truth at the packet's tick, not at the tick the packet arrived. 9471363 delivered states were compared against the ground truth and 0 mismatched; 0 mirror mismatches.
